summary: Death insurance: if you would fail a Deadline you get 2 extra Rounds to pay instead. Breaks after it saves you.
tip: Once you have drawers, keep it in one and equip it during the death countdown so it never wastes a slot.

synergies.why: Fuses with Ankh into Ra's Book (DLC), a death save that can pay the whole debt.
Vorago bans the Ankh when it breaks; sell Vorago later to get a fresh Ankh back.
Its self-discard counts as a discard for Dung Beetle.
Fuses with Ankh into Resurrection (DLC), which brings charms discarded during a Round back to the store.
Each bonus Round can take up to 21 spins, so the save is worth more than a whole normal Deadline.

antiSynergies.why: Rounds only have 1 spin, so the 2 bonus Rounds are just 2 spins.

summary: Doubles the activation chance of every charm with 'Triggers randomly' (D4, Fake Coin, Peppers, Rosary, Broken Calculator...).
tip: Only worth a slot with 2+ random-trigger charms. Best partners: Fake Coin (more spins) and D4.

synergies.why: 10% becomes 20%: roughly one or two bonus spins with Luck+4 per Round.
30% becomes 60% chance to reroll symbols outside Patterns.
35% becomes 70% chance to retrigger every Pattern.
35% becomes 70% chance to cancel a 666.
Luck+7 fires twice as often (it also burns its 9 uses faster).
With Nuclear Button and Sacred Heart, fuses into Glorious Trumpet (DLC).

summary: Red Button (2 charges): every 'Triggers randomly' charm is guaranteed to fire on the next spin. Small break chance if used 5+ times in a Round.
tip: Spend charges on key spins: guarantee Rosary before a risky spin, Fake Coin for a free spin, or Broken Calculator on a high-Luck spin.

effects.text: Red Button: every equipped 'Triggers randomly' charm activates on the next spin, if its own condition allows.
When used 5 or more times in the same Round, each use has a 10% chance to discard this charm.

synergies.why: Each activation guarantees its bonus spin with Luck+4; overcharged, you stay spin-neutral.
Fire it before a risky spin to guarantee a 666 is cancelled.
Guarantees a retrigger on the spin you choose, ideally a high-Luck one.
Guarantees a reroll of non-pattern symbols on the chosen spin.
Each press banks two guaranteed activations.
When it breaks, Vorago bans it; discarding Vorago brings back a fresh Golden Horseshoe.

assumptions: Charms with their own conditions (Dynamo at Round end, Consolation Prize on blank spins) only fire if that condition is met.
Break roll assumed to apply to each use from the 5th one in a Round; banked extra activations are lost if it breaks.

summary: Every Pattern triggers one extra time on the first spin of each Round.
tip: Cheap steady retrigger. Press Red Shiny Rock before the first spin; with the Fixation memory card every spin is a first spin.

synergies.why: Both Hamsas fuse into 10 Fingers Hamsa (DLC).
Use its Luck+4 on the first spin so the doubled spin is a big one.
Every Round is a single spin, so Hamsa doubles every spin.
Doubled Patterns on the first spin help reach Pentacle's 5+ threshold.

antiSynergies.why: Only one Round per Deadline, so it fires once every ~21 spins.

summary: Luck+7 on the last spin of every Round, which usually turns that spin into a multi-Pattern hit.
tip: Strong early pick. If you gain a bonus spin after the last spin (Fake Coin, Ancient Coin), the new last spin gets Luck+7 again.

synergies.why: Both Hamsas fuse into 10 Fingers Hamsa (DLC).
Every Round is a single spin, so every spin gets Luck+7.
Used on the last spin, its extra Luck+7 spin also gets Rotated Hamsa's Luck+7.
A bonus spin after the last spin triggers Luck+7 a second time.

antiSynergies.why: Only one Round per Deadline, so only one boosted spin in ~21.

summary: Whenever a spin triggers 7+ Patterns (retriggers count), you earn twice your current Interest in coins. Max once per spin.
tip: Needs retriggers or heavy Luck to reach 7+; raise Interest with Stonks or Grandma's Purse. With Lucky and Swole Cat it fuses into Cosmic Cat (DLC).

synergies.why: With Lucky Cat and Swole Cat, fuses into Cosmic Cat (DLC).
+5% Interest raises every payout.
+15% Interest for a few Rounds makes each payout much bigger.
A Round of doubled yellow Patterns makes 7+ Pattern spins much more likely.
A permanent extra trigger on every Pattern doubles your count.

summary: Whenever a spin triggers 15+ Patterns (retriggers count), you earn 4x your current Interest in coins. Max once per spin.
tip: Only for heavy retrigger builds: even a Jackpot is about 10 Patterns. Otherwise it is mainly a piece of the Cosmic Cat fusion (DLC).

synergies.why: With Lucky Cat and Chonky Cat, fuses into Cosmic Cat (DLC).
Its Round of extra yellow triggers can lift a Jackpot or big Luck spin past 15 Patterns.
Doubled Number 1/2 presses stack extra Pattern triggers toward 15+.
A permanent extra trigger on every Pattern doubles your count.
+5% Interest makes each 4x payout bigger.

summary: Gives one guaranteed Jackpot in the next Round, then breaks.
tip: A cheap bailout often worth a big chunk of a Deadline. Pair with I can't quit now! (x2 Jackpot value) or keep Vorago to get it back.

synergies.why: Doubles the Jackpot pattern's own value, adding about a quarter to the free Jackpot spin (the other ~9 Patterns are unchanged).
The Jackpot spin has ~10 Patterns, doubling Symbol values for the rest of the Round.
A Jackpot alone is ~10 Patterns, enough to trigger it.
Vorago bans the Pony when it breaks; sell Vorago to get it back for another Jackpot.
Its self-discard counts as a discard for Dung Beetle.

assumptions: Assumed the Jackpot lands on the first spin of the next Round; encoded as a first-spin Jackpot with the charm gone after that one Round, so exactly one Jackpot is counted.

summary: Red Button (1 charge): Luck+4 on the next spin. Recharges every Round, so you get one use per Round.
tip: Use it on Hamsa's first spin or on your last spin. Left full, it lets Super Capacitor feed your other button charms. Cheap early filler.

synergies.why: Luck+4 on the first spin makes Hamsa's doubled spin bigger.
A full 1-charge charm donates a charge to another button charm every spin.
Each press gives Luck+8 instead of Luck+4.
Pressed before the last spin, its Luck+4 stacks with Luck+7 for Luck+11.

summary: Symbols Multiplier that grows by 1 each spin a charm triggers and drops back to 0 after any spin where no charm triggers.
tip: Needs charms that fire on most spins (Lucky Cat, Horseshoe-boosted D4 or Broken Calculator); one spin with no charm trigger wipes the bonus.

effects.text: The accumulated bonus resets to 0 after any spin in which no Lucky Charm triggers.

synergies.why: Doubles random triggers so fewer spins pass with no charm firing.
Fires on 35% of spins (70% with Horseshoe), keeping the streak alive, and retriggers Patterns too.
Fires on 30% of spins, helping keep the streak going.
Triggers on every 3+ Pattern spin, extending the streak.

assumptions: Assumed +1 per spin in which at least one charm triggers, not +1 per charm.
Unclear which activations count as a trigger; passive charms like Stonks probably do not.
reset:round is the closest allowed value: the real reset is after any spin with no charm trigger (often sooner), though a streak can carry into the next Round.

summary: Each other charm you discard (sell) or that breaks adds +1x base value to all Symbols, as long as the Beetle stays on the table.
tip: Buy cheap charms and sell them to grow it. Fidelity Card, the Sacrifices card and charms that break on their own speed it up.

effects.text: The bonus only applies while Dung Beetle is equipped; only discards made while it is on the table count, and progress carries over to a re-bought Dung Beetle.

synergies.why: Cheaper charms make cheaper discard fodder.
A permanent store discount makes buy-and-sell fodder cheap.
With Corpse pieces it spawns free charms every Deadline to discard.
A 1-ticket charm that breaks by itself, adding a stack.
Higher resell values refund more tickets when you sell fodder.

summary: +15% Interest that drops by 3% after each Round; it breaks after 5 Rounds when the bonus reaches 0.
tip: Buy it when you can deposit early or run Lucky/Chonky Cat or Token modifiers. Vorago can bring a fresh one back after it breaks.

synergies.why: Each 3+ Pattern spin pays out your boosted Interest.
Its double-Interest payouts get much bigger.
Stacks to 27% Interest in the first Round.
Vorago bans it when it runs out; sell Vorago for a fresh +15% Purse.
Breaking by itself counts as a discard.

summary: +2 charm space. It uses one slot itself, so you net one extra charm slot.
tip: Almost always worth 2 tickets. Covers the -1 space of Nuclear Button, Megaphone or Hourglass; fuses with Sardines into Beach Hotel (DLC).

synergies.why: Fuses with Sardines into Beach Hotel (+3 space, DLC).
Pays for Nuclear Button's -1 charm space.
Pays for Megaphone's -1 charm space.
Pays for Hourglass's -1 charm space.

summary: Every Red Button charm triggers one extra time per press, doubling its effect; -1 charm space.
tip: Take it once you run 2+ strong Red Button charms (Number 1/2, Midas Touch, pictures). Core of overcharging with AA Batteries.

synergies.why: Each press adds two extra triggers to yellow Patterns for the Round.
Each press doubles the permanent gain per scored symbol.
Battery recharges plus doubled presses are the core of overcharging.
Each press grants two extra spins with Luck+7.
Covers the -1 charm space.
With Horseshoe and Sacred Heart, fuses into Glorious Trumpet (DLC).

summary: The telephone offers one extra ability to choose from (4 instead of 3).
tip: With drawers, keep it stored and equip it just before answering the phone. Fuses with Fidelity Card into VIP Card (DLC).

synergies.why: More options to find an ability worth doubling.
Pick the best of four, then trigger it again later with Barathrum.
Abilities trigger twice with this card, so picking the right one matters more.
Fuses with Fidelity Card into VIP Card (DLC).

summary: After every spin, each fully charged Red Button charm you have gives 1 charge to another random equipped charm.
tip: Keep a 1-charge charm like Red Shiny Rock or Ancient Coin full so it donates a charge every spin to Number 1/2 or Midas Touch.

effects.text: Repeats once per fully charged equipped Red Button charm after each spin; each charge goes to another random equipped charm.

synergies.why: Left full, this 1-charge charm donates a charge every spin.
Another 1-charge charm that can sit full and feed the others.
Turns spare charges into frequent 5-charge Number 1 Rounds.
Refills Midas Touch's 4 charges much faster.
Lower charge costs leave more charms full and donating.
With Dynamo, Potato Battery and Electricity Meter, fuses into Exotic Matter (DLC).

assumptions: Assumed the donated charge goes to a Red Button charm that is not full; if it can land on a full or non-button charm it is wasted.

summary: At the end of each Round, 40% chance to restore 1 charge to every equipped Red Button charm.
tip: Worth it with several high-charge button charms (Number 1/2, Midas Touch, pictures). Horseshoe raises it to 80%.

synergies.why: 40% becomes 80% per Round.
Speeds up refilling its 4 charges.
Speeds up refilling its 5 charges.
With Super Capacitor, Potato Battery and Electricity Meter, fuses into Exotic Matter (DLC).

summary: Your most likely symbol appears more often (+1 chance); ties all get it, so at the start both Lemons and Cherries are boosted.
tip: Great in any one-symbol build: push your main symbol to the top with a picture or phone call and this adds +1 more on top.

synergies.why: Fuses with Expired Meds into Magic Potion (DLC).
Makes Sevens the most likely symbol, so Sevens get +1 more.
One +1 Seven call makes Sevens the most likely symbol for good.
Lemons start tied for most likely, so they get +1 and gild more often.

summary: +5% Interest (7% to 12% at base), paid on your deposit at the end of every Round.
tip: Small on its own; take it when Cats or Token modifiers turn Interest into coins during spins.

synergies.why: Every Lucky Cat payout grows with your Interest.
Its double-Interest payouts grow too.
Token symbols pay half your Interest each, so +5% boosts them.

summary: Instantly refills every equipped Red Button charm to full charge. Doesn't take a slot.
tip: Buy it when your expensive button charms (Number 1/2, Midas Touch, Weird Clock) are empty. Abyssu can store it for later.

synergies.why: Refills its 4 charges for another permanent-gain Round.
Refills its 5 charges for another Round of yellow retriggers.
Refills all 12 charges for another bonus Round.
Bank it in Abyssu and fire it when your best button charm is empty.
Overdose stops the round-end recharge, so a full refill is worth far more.

summary: Your most valuable symbol never appears (Sevens at the start); symbols tied for most valuable are all banned.
tip: Early it removes Sevens and slightly raises pattern odds, but sell it before your main symbol becomes your most valuable one or it gets banned.

synergies.why: Fuses with Scratch and Hope into Magic Potion (DLC).

antiSynergies.why: Sevens are what it bans at the start, so gilded Sevens never show up.
Pumping your main symbol makes it the most valuable, and then it gets banned.
Extra Seven chance is wasted while Sevens are banned.
Its gains push Diamonds and Treasures past Sevens as most valuable, so both get banned.

summary: Red Button (4 charges): for the rest of the Round every scored symbol permanently gains its base value, as if all symbols were Golden.
tip: Fire it on Rounds with Luck or retriggers. Nuclear Button, Number 1/2 and battery recharges turn it into huge permanent growth.

synergies.why: Each press gives two base-value gains per scored symbol.
Retriggered Patterns score their symbols again, multiplying the gains.
Battery recharges let you fire it again in the same Round.
Turns full 1-charge charms into Midas Touch charges.
An instant refill for another Midas Touch Round.
Fuses with Consolation Prize into First Place Prize (DLC).

antiSynergies.why: The symbol you pump becomes the most valuable and gets banned.

assumptions: Red Button symbolValue/addBase with duration round means: every symbol scored during the activated Round permanently gains its base value (per symbol scored, retriggers included), like Golden on everything.

summary: Red Button (5 charges): for the rest of the Round, Patterns of yellow symbols (Lemon, Bell, Treasure, Seven) trigger one extra time.
tip: Fire it at the start of a Round. With AA Batteries on Bells and Nuclear Button you can recharge and stack it mid-Round (overcharging).

synergies.why: Battery Bells recharge it mid-Round so you can stack it again.
Each press adds two extra triggers instead of one.
More Bells means more yellow Patterns and more Battery recharges.
Retriggers multiply Midas Touch's permanent gains.
Feeds its 5 charges far faster.

summary: Red Button (5 charges): for the rest of the Round, Patterns of non-yellow symbols (Cherry, Clover, Diamond) trigger one extra time.
tip: Fire it at the start of a Round. With AA Batteries on Clovers and Nuclear Button you can recharge and stack it mid-Round (overcharging).

synergies.why: Battery Clovers recharge it mid-Round so you can stack it again.
Each press adds two extra triggers instead of one.
More Clovers means more non-yellow Patterns and more Battery recharges.
Retriggers multiply Midas Touch's permanent gains.
Feeds its 5 charges far faster.

summary: When a spin shows exactly one Pattern, its symbols turn into your most valuable symbol (Sevens at the start).
tip: Best when your most valuable symbol is rare, like pumped Sevens; Little Star's forced HOR-XL is a great target. Weak if your common symbol is also your best.

synergies.why: The forced HOR-XL after a blank spin is often the only Pattern, so it becomes your best symbol.
Sevens are rare but most valuable; gilding them makes every conversion pay more.
Tripling Seven value makes each converted Pattern worth far more.

assumptions: Assumed the converted Pattern scores with the new symbol; which symbol is used when several tie for most valuable is unknown.

summary: +1 Patterns Multiplier for every 15 Clover Tickets you are holding.
tip: A ticket-hoarding payoff: pair with Cloverpot, Cloverpet and Ticket modifiers. Avoid phone calls that set tickets to 0.

synergies.why: Grows your ticket pile every Deadline.
The same ticket pile also feeds Cloverpet's Symbols Multiplier.
Ticket modifiers keep a big ticket stack coming.
Doubling your tickets can add several multiplier steps at once.

antiSynergies.why: No tickets from Rounds makes 15-ticket steps hard to hold.

summary: Instantly gives coins equal to 30% of the current Deadline's debt. Doesn't take a slot.
tip: Always worth 30% of the debt, so it matters most when you are falling short; also a bailout during the death countdown. Abyssu can bank it.

synergies.why: Bank it in Abyssu as an emergency 30% payment for a bad Deadline.
Paying 30% of the debt up front helps you finish early and skip Rounds.

assumptions: Assumed 30% of the full debt of the current Deadline, not of the unpaid remainder.

summary: At the end of each Deadline, permanently gain +1 Symbols Multiplier per Round you skipped, plus 1.
tip: Pay debts early to skip Rounds; each skip also gives 4 tickets. Shares the skip plan with Greedy King and Golden Pepper.

synergies.why: Also grows from skipped Rounds; skip early to grow both.
Also rewards skipping: +4 Luck per Round skipped in the previous Deadline.
30% of the debt up front makes skipping Rounds easier.
7 one-spin Rounds per Deadline: once the debt is paid, every Round left can be skipped for +1.

antiSynergies.why: Only one Round per Deadline leaves almost nothing to skip.

assumptions: The '+1' at the end of the official text is read as a flat +1 every Deadline; the item's own wiki page omits it, so it may only be +1 per skipped Round.
Only Rounds skipped while you own it count; the game adds the bonus when the Deadline ends (encoded as growth per skipped Round).

summary: After a spin with no Patterns, the next spin is guaranteed a HOR-XL across the middle row.
tip: A big early-game floor since about half of early spins are blank. Pairs with Pain Killers and Abstract Painting; it breaks the no-reward streaks trains need.

synergies.why: The forced HOR-XL is often the only Pattern, so it turns into your best symbol.
The 5-symbol HOR-XL doubles all Pattern values for the rest of the Round.
The HOR-XL counts as a 4+ Pattern, raising all Patterns for the Round.
Each forced HOR-XL is a 4+ Pattern that grows Diamonds and Treasures.

antiSynergies.why: It never lets 2 spins in a row go without reward.
Breaks the 3-spin no-reward streak it needs.
Breaks the 3-spin no-reward streak it needs.
Breaks the 2-spin no-reward streak it needs.

assumptions: noRewardStreak:1 stands for 'the previous spin scored no Patterns'; the forced row's symbol is assumed to be rolled by normal symbol chances.

summary: Instantly restocks the store with charms whose effect mentions Luck (Peppers, Rotated Hamsa, Fake Coin...). Doesn't take a slot.
tip: A 1-ticket targeted reroll for Luck builds. Restock-triggered charms like Bell Pepper do not count it as a restock.

effects.text: Restocks the store with charms that have Luck in their effect; boxes it cannot fill get normal charms.

synergies.why: One of the best Luck charms it can dig up.
A cheap Luck charm with bonus spins it can find.
Makes the Peppers it finds trigger twice as often.
